verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT), concluding a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R3: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on Friday ... off the Southern California coast shortly after 5:07 p.m. Pacific Time ... after nearly 10 days'; R4: 'splashdown ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (0007 GMT on April 11)'; R5: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. ET ... 10-day journey'; R1: 'splashdown on April 10 ... about nine and a half days'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm exact date, time, location, success, and ~10-day duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew did not land on the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Artemis crew will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead, the plan is to loop around it'; R3: 'traveling ... a climactic lunar flyby some 4,000 miles from its surface'; R4: 'never left the crew capsule. Instead they only observed the moon from space'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state no landing on the moon, only flyby.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew successfully flew around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'loop around it, getting an unprecedented view of the far side of the moon'; R2: 'carrying NASA astronauts ... on an approximate 10-day mission around the Moon and back'; R3: 'journey around the far side of the moon'; R4: '10-day journey around the moon and back'; R5: 'historic journey around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm successful flyby/loop around the moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew safely returned to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The Artemis II crew is safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'safely splashed down ... all four astronauts were in good shape'; R4: 'safely retrieved ... All four crew members ... back'; R5: 'safely back on Earth ... Four green crewmembers'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state safe return and crew in good condition post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule, named Integrity, splashed down in the Pacific Ocean near California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Orion capsule, dubbed Integrity, parachuted gently into ... Pacific Ocean ... off the Southern California coast'; R2: 'Orion spacecraft ... splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'Orion capsule Integrity ... splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm name 'Integrity' and splashdown location off California/San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consisted of four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; similar in R3,R4,R5
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exactly four astronauts by name.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew completed their 10-day journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'From launch ... to splashdown on April 10, the mission is slated to last about nine and a half days'; R2: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R3: 'nearly 10 days in space'; R4: '10-day journey'; R5: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe as ~10-day mission successfully completed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission included the first human flyby of the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R3: 'first voyage by humans to the vicinity of the moon in over half a century'; R4: 'first humans in over 50 years to venture to the Moon'; R5: 'first humans in over 50 years to venture to the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed lunar flyby/mission in 50+ years since Apollo.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts were safely retrieved by the US Navy after splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'U.S. helicopters ... to the USS John P. Murtha ... U.S. Navy helicopters'; R3: 'U.S. Navy recovery teams ... hoisted ... to helicopters ... to a nearby Navy amphibious transport vessel, the John P. Murtha'; R4: 'Navy divers ... hoisted one by one to helicopters ... USS John P. Murtha'; R5: 'Navy recovery ship ... helicopters ... USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm safe US Navy retrieval via helicopters to USS John P. Murtha.
